title: VoyageReplay scenario (.voyage.json)
description: A timestamped reconstruction of a marine incident or manoeuvre, sufficient to replay it in 3D from any participant's viewpoint. Format version 0.1 is UNSTABLE and may change without a migration.

formatVersion.description: Semver-ish version of this format. 0.x is unstable.

occurredAt.description: ISO 8601 with offset. For a collision, the moment of contact.

timeZone.description: IANA zone the human-readable clock in this scenario refers to.

locality.description: Free text, e.g. 'Suo-nada, off Nojima, Yamaguchi'.

license.description: Terms the underlying source data is reproduced under.

origin.description: Geodetic origin of the local tangent plane. All rendering happens in metres east/north of this point, so it should sit near the action - a few kilometres out, the flat-earth error is far below the precision of the source data.

lightCondition.description: Whether navigation lights would be exhibited and visible. 'night' and 'restricted-visibility' both mean lights are shown.

visibilityMetres.description: Meteorological visibility. null when the source does not state it.

current.description: Set (degrees true, the direction the water flows TOWARD) and drift (knots).

derivation.description: Where this figure came from. This is the claim the reconstruction rests on, so it is required rather than optional: 'measured' is a recording, 'digitised' was read off a plotted chart, 'inferred' was reconstructed from testimony or narrative, 'interpolated' was computed by this tool between other points.

citation.description: Human-readable pointer precise enough to check by hand, e.g. 'Appendix table 1, p.14'.

id.description: Stable within the scenario. Reports usually anonymise as A / B; keep that.

kind.description: Discriminator. Only 'vessel' is implemented; the field exists so other actor kinds can be added without a format break.

type.description: Drives which lights are exhibited and the default hull shape.

referencePointOffsets.description: Where the reported position actually sits on the hull. AIS message 5 carries exactly these four distances, and JTSB appendix tables restate them in a footnote - so a track reported at the GPS antenna can be moved to the ship's centre without guessing.

positionAt.description: What the lat/lon in each point refers to. AIS reports the GPS antenna, which on a 180 m ship is over a hundred metres from the bow - close enough to matter when the question is whether the hulls touched.

t.description: ISO 8601 with offset. Verbose on purpose: a reconstruction is checked by a human against a report that prints wall-clock times.

cogDegreesTrue.description: Course over ground. Where the ship is GOING.

headingDegreesTrue.description: Where the bow POINTS. Absent whenever the source could not supply it - a Class B AIS transponder does not transmit heading at all, and half of a two-ship reconstruction typically lacks it. Do not silently substitute cogDegreesTrue: the difference is the drift angle, and in a tideway it is visible.

derivation.description: Overrides the track's derivation for this point alone.
